definition: The first edition of the textbook Data Science and Predictive Analytics: Biomedical and Health Applications using R, authored by Ivo D.
details: Dinov, was published in August 2018 by Springer. The second edition of the book was printed in 2023. This textbook covers some of the core mathematical foundations, computational techniques, and artificial intelligence approaches used in data science research and applications. By using the statistical computing platform R and a broad range of biomedical case-studies, the 23 chapters of the book first edition provide explicit examples of importing, exporting, processing, modeling, visualizing, and interpreting large, multivariate, incomplete, heterogeneous, longitudinal, and incomplete datasets (big data).

explainer.lead: Data Science and Predictive Analytics is Ivo D. Dinov’s textbook on using mathematics, computation, and artificial intelligence to learn from complex data. Its R examples and biomedical case studies show how raw health data can be processed, modeled, visualized, and interpreted.

tiers.eli5: Think of health data as a huge, messy box of puzzle pieces, with some pieces missing and others looking very different. This book is like a guide to sorting those pieces with R, finding patterns, making pictures, and explaining what the patterns might mean.
tiers.practitioner: An analyst can use the book as an R-based reference for importing, exporting, processing, modeling, visualizing, and interpreting large biomedical datasets. Its examples address multivariate, incomplete, heterogeneous, and longitudinal data, but demonstrations should not be confused with ready-made production or clinical systems.
tiers.paperLevel: The textbook connects core mathematical foundations, computational techniques, and artificial intelligence approaches through R-based biomedical case studies. Ivo D. Dinov’s first edition, published by Springer in August 2018, contains 23 chapters; the second edition was printed in 2023.

explainer.example: A researcher could import a longitudinal patient dataset into R, process its missing and mixed measurements, fit a model, plot measurements over time, and interpret the resulting patterns rather than treating the model output as self-explanatory.

explainer.intuition: The central idea is to turn difficult, messy data into understandable evidence through a connected sequence of computation, modeling, visualization, and interpretation. Biomedical examples make that sequence concrete while R supplies the tools.
howItWorks: Import data into R, or export results for further use.
Process large datasets that may be multivariate, incomplete, heterogeneous, or longitudinal.
Apply mathematical, computational, and artificial intelligence techniques to model the data.
Visualize the data and modeling results to reveal patterns.
Interpret the results in the context of biomedical and health applications.
explainer.whyItMatters: Large health datasets are rarely clean or uniform, so useful analysis requires more than applying a predictive model. The book emphasizes the full path from data handling to interpretation.
misconceptions: It is a textbook, not a software package or a single predictive algorithm.
Predictive modeling is only one part; processing, visualization, and interpretation are also central.
R is the platform used for the examples, not the subject of the title itself.
